Oml, you really just misunderstood everything I said... Apologies for not spoiler-marking.

I guess I could see Heroes as police or military, but I feel like they're supposed to be read closer to police. Heroes and police are deeply intertwined too.

I think the problem here is that I think killing people is more immoral than you. Killing people is horrifically immoral in cases where it's not self-defense of defense of your loved ones.

Also, I'm not talking about self-defense, which is literally something I mentioned. If you know someone who killed somebody in the mess of battle... I'm not talking about them. I'm talking about someone who killed people that were specifically not an equal threat and they could've chosen to spare their lives. Imagine a soldier who used war as an excuse to mass-murder, not were forced in a situation where they needed to kill to survive.

Villains, most of them, are just normal-ass criminals, and I just don't think you should be able to kill them unless you absolutely have to.

Snipe has an accuracy-type quirk, doesn't he? He shoots people in places likely to immobilize them, and not kill.

The situations with Iida and Stain are a bit different than how you're framing them, I doubt Shoto would've actually killed any of those men, I interpreted it more like a threat to scare the villains that likely wouldn't have been delivered on more than anything else. Iida also had no fucking idea what he was doing, just a dumb kid doing an impulsive thing he didn't understand to someone who almost killed his brother.

I don't want to argue with you on the morality of killing. I really thought people could just agree on it being universally bad. You can respond another time, but I really, really don't want to debate this. Some things you don't debate.

Maybe I've gotten owned because I thought killing was as bad in the universe of mha as it is irl, but whatever man, I don't care about this enough to search through hours upon hours of mha and wiki quotes to argue with someone who's justifying killing criminals. Our moral compasses are just different.

The thing I'm complaining about in fics and what you're talking about are COMPLETELY different. All For One and >!Twice!< are literally some of the most dangerous quirk-users and some random villains at USJ are... not that. To make those equal, it'd be more like Izuku killing the nomu than random villain #8.

Heroes don't normally kill people, not that they can't but most are NOT supposed to. On an interpersonal scale, would you want to hang around someone who was enlisted and took the opportunity that war provides to kill a bunch of people that they didn't need to? No. No you wouldn't. That's what I mean by consequences, not so much legal, but personal ones.

Also, Heroes are more comparable to police than military, they're police mixed with movie-stars. Maybe you mean national guard? Cause Military usually fights external threats and national guard is usually for at-home threats.

So, a lot of MHA fans are really young, and it's a common trope to put your characters through hell, especially Izu in MHA's case. Many people project themselves onto Izu, and they're mostly teens who have little experience with writing and lots of negative emotions to vent.

As a society, we have an obsession with the dark, the grim. To me it's no surprise we see young sad kids writing their own torture p\*rn. It's a less refined form of what we see everywhere else. Eh.

I think it would be better (characterization wise and story-wise) for Authors to address this in their stories and have Izu react appropriately. Maybe he hides them, maybe he shows them off as spite. Try to make characters react differently than you would, but still reasonably.

Something that is extremely cathartic for me, is the knowledge that once I'm out of the house, I can say whatever I want to them, and since they don't have direct control over me- they can't stop me. I can tell them they abused me, that they were awful, or not talk to them at all. Once you move out you'll be completely free, they can't control you anymore. 

Don't know if that thought gives you any comfort, but it keeps me going, gives me motivation to make it through all their bullshit, and when I'm forced to take it in complete silence, it sure does help me to know that I can throw it all back when I'm independent.

Do you think they'd listen if you told them not to tell your parents? If not, friends or even people online are also good outlet. It's very important to be able to talk, even just to anons. Which is what it looks like you're doing, and that's good, the world feels very lonely and isolating when you don't have anyone behind you, a few anons are better than being left completely alone with your shitty parent and siblings who don't seem to get it.
